means: A bright edge of light tracing the OUTLINE of the figure - the top of the hair, the line of a shoulder, the edge of a jaw - because the source sits behind the subject. It draws the outside of a person, not the front of them.
does: Paints a hard bright line along hair and shoulder edges and lets the front of the subject fall a stop darker, which peels the character off the background. It lands because it names a THING the model can draw (a bright edge) rather than a property of the air. What does NOT land is the DEGREE: light.rim ships six grades (none/subtle/strong/halo/kiss/double_rim) and the measured panel sweep classes that card RECOMPOSED at layout spread 35.83, meaning the option clause re-rolled the whole shot rather than dialling the edge up and down. Treat it as on/off; if you want it stronger, add backlighting rather than an adjective.
reach_for_it: when a character is sinking into a busy or same-value background and has to read as a separate shape - and on any shot where character consistency matters, because an outlined figure survives a reroll better than a face does
used_in: studio/lighting/rim.json (key 'rim lighting, backlit', rim 0.9) and studio/lighting/backlit.json (rim 0.85); studio/cards/light_rim.json sweeps six grades
